 10 Masterpiece Movies Better Than The Dark Knight
 Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne standing in front of the batsuit in The Dark Knight. Image via Warner Bros. Pictures 
 Add CBR on Google 
 Add as Preferred Source 
 Follow on Google Discover 
 By  
 Maxwell Pishny 
 Published Oct 24, 2026, 5:00 PM EDT 
 Having spent over two decades obsessed with all things superheroes and comic books, Max continues to put just about all his time into engaging with art of all kinds -- film, television, music, novels, and of course, comics. Max loves to draw, especially comic characters. In fact, that's what got him excited about the medium in the first place. From the moment he could hold a crayon, he was drawing Batman, Spider-Man, or Superman on any surface he could get his hands on. Comics opened Max's mind up to the greater art-world as a whole, he is eternally grateful for that.
A completionist at heart, Max has read over 5,000 individual comic issues, and that number grows every day at an alarming rate. His latest major undertaking is reading every published Batman book since 1986 -- a project which he knows will take quite some time.

 Christopher Nolan's 2008 masterpiece, The Dark Knight , changed mainstream movies forever. It is, without a doubt, one of the single most important blockbusters ever made, and it stands as one of the very best comic book movies of all time. However, despite its brilliance, there are still quite a few movies better than The Dark Knight .

 Ranging across genres, time periods, and franchises, these 10 movie masterpieces stand above The Dark Knight in just about every way. Nolan's 2008 epic is certainly an all-time classic, but these movies are, against all odds, even better.
 No Country for Old Men Is A Harrowing Crime Thriller
 One of the greatest aspects of The Dark Knight is Heath Ledger's legendary performance as the Joker. Ledger's Joker instantly became one of cinema's greatest on-screen villains , and his impact is still felt today. Another film that features one of the best modern cinematic villains is 2007's No Country for Old Men , directed by Joel and Ethan Coen.
 The Coen brothers are some of the most exciting directors in American movie history, and No Country for Old Men might just be their greatest achievement. Based on the Cormac McCarthy novel of the same name, No Country for Old Men is a thrilling, genuinely unsettling tale of greed, evil, and moral decay, and it's far superior to The Dark Knight .
 The Godfather Is An-All Time Classic Gangster Flick
 Marlon Brando as Vito Corleone in The Godfather's opening scene. Image via Paramount Pictures 
 Without the influence of masterpieces like The Godfather , there's a good chance that The Dark Knight would not exist today. Director Francis Ford Coppola utterly redefined the world of on-screen organized crime with his 1972 masterpiece, and the cinematic world owes so much to his groundbreaking efforts.
 The Godfather is the type of film that, despite being heralded as an all-time great for decades, really does live up to the hype. Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, John Cazale, and Diane Keaton are all spectacular in the film, and its mastery of the cinematic art form is better than so many films that came in its wake.
 The Batman Is The Superior Adaptation For The Character
 Robert Pattinson in the cape and cowl in The Batman Image via Warner Bros. Pictures 
 The debate between whether Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight or Matt Reeves' The Batman is the superior adaptation of the iconic comic book character has raged for years since the latter released in theaters, and while there's certainly an argument to be made in Nolan's favor, The Batman does surpass The Dark Knight in almost every way .
 A darker, more introspective take on Batman, Matt Reeves' film took the focus away from the villains and put it squarely on the title character himself, allowing Robert Pattinson to give audiences the best live-action Batman performance ever. The film is a pitch-perfect crime thriller, and it's the best DC Comics adaptation ever.
 North by Northwest Is A Timeless Mystery Thriller
 Cary Grant flees from a plane in North by Northwest Image via Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer 
 One of the legendary Alfred Hitchcock's very best films , 1959's North by Northwest is the sort of movie that, like The Godfather , shouldn't live up to the hype, but absolutely does. Starring the iconic Cary Grant in one of his very best roles, North by Northwest is a top-to-bottom masterpiece that boasts some of the greatest set pieces in movie history.
 A classic "wrong man" Hitchcock thriller, North by Northwest effortlessly bounces between hilarious and harrowing, all while consistently keeping the audience guessing about the reality of its mysteries. A visual treat that shows exactly why Hitchcock has remained so legendary for all these years, North by Northwest is impossible not to love, and nearly impossible to beat.
 Se7en Is A Terrifying Serial Killer Masterpiece
 Morgan Freeman as William Somerset in Se7en Image via  New Line Cinema and FilmFlex 
 Before director David Fincher redefined serial killer stories forever with his 2007 true-crime masterpiece, Zodiac , he gave the sub-genre one of its best with 1995's Se7en . Starring Brad Pitt and Morgan Freeman as two police detectives on the trail of a serial murderer whose kills are modeled after the Seven Deadly Sins, Se7en is a spine-tingling masterclass in tension-building.
 Featuring one of the most shocking twists in movie history , as well as some of the finest performances in the crime thriller genre, Se7en immediately cemented David Fincher as one of the most exciting names in contemporary Hollywood. It's an all-time masterpiece, and one of the films that really does beat out The Dark Knight .

 Blade Runner Is An Atmospheric Sci-Fi Opus
 Blade Runner still Image via Warner Bros. 
 The definitive entry in the cyberpunk sub-genre, Ridley Scott's 1982 masterpiece, Blade Runner , is absolutely staggering to behold. Without Blade Runner , the science fiction genre today would look vastly different, and its impact has been felt for decades even outside its specific genre.
 Blade Runner sees Harrison Ford taking on the role of Rick Deckard, a police officer tasked with hunting down artificial humans known as replicants. What follows is one of the most introspective, astounding explorations of humanity, reality, and existence ever put to screen.
 Manhunter Is A Superbly Frightening Mystery Masterpiece
 Will Graham in Manhunter Image via De Laurentiis Entertainment Group 
 Directed by the legendary Michael Mann, 1986's Manhunter is the best Hannibal Lecter movie of all time , even narrowly beating out Jonathan Demme's masterpiece, The Silence of the Lambs . Based on Thomas Harris's iconic Red Dragon novel, Manhunter sees Special Agent Will Graham tracking down a terrifying new serial killer.
 A superb tone and mood piece unlike any other, Manhunter is one of the most enthralling crime pictures of the 1980s, and one of the most underrated movies in the genre's entire history. William Petersen is astonishing in the lead role, and supporting performances from legends like Tom Noonan, Dennis Farina, and Brian Cox only make Manhunter even more of a must-watch.
 Blow Out Is A Pitch-Perfect Conspiracy Thriller
 John Travolta as Jack Terry holding a phone to his face in Blow Out Image via Filmways Pictures 
 Director Brian De Palma might have taken immense influence from the iconic Alfred Hitchcock , but he consistently made films that felt uniquely his own, and none showcase that fact better than Blow Out . Starring John Travolta as a movie sound technician who accidentally records evidence of a political assassination, the 1981 masterpiece is a must-watch for any crime movie fan.
 A visual and auditory feast, Blow Out features Travolta at his very best, and the pulpy nature of its central mystery is impossible not to get swept away in. The film's finale is one of the most shocking endings in movie history, and it has remained an all-time masterpiece in the conspiracy thriller sub-genre for decades.
 Interstellar Is Christopher Nolan's Best Movie
 Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) walks on an alien planet in Interstellar Image via Warner Bros/Everett Collection 
 Many movie fans point to The Dark Knight as Nolan's greatest achievement , but he topped himself just 6 years later with 2014's Interstellar . A cosmic odyssey like no other, Interstellar is the kind of era-defining movie that must be seen to be believed. Nolan's most emotionally impactful film, as well as his most ambitious, Interstellar is truly perfect.
 The Dark Knight is a masterpiece, but Interstellar is something even greater. Visually, thematically, and narratively, Interstellar is unlike any other film made in the last 40 years. It's the ultimate proof of Nolan's spectacular talent, and it has only gotten better in the years since its initial theatrical release.
 Heat Is The Ultimate Blueprint For The Dark Knight
 Robert de Niro sits at a dinner table across from Al Pacino in Michael Mann's Heat Image via Warner Bros 
 Anyone who has seen both The Dark Knight and Heat knows that the former would not exist without the latter. Micheal Mann's 1995 masterpiece is one of the most influential crime flicks of all time , and its visual style, tactical feel, and sprawling narrative are all clear points of reference for Christopher Nolan's Batman movie.
 Simply put, Heat is a miracle of contemporary moviemaking. Its action is flawless, its character work is unrivaled, and its bombastic runtime makes it feel truly epic. So many modern action movies would not exist without the masterpiece that is Heat , and The Dark Knight is one of the biggest examples.
